0.0.n: Sets the time for the cooking demonstration.

0.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic: what happens today.

0.2.n: A place name; 県 means prefecture.

0.3.n: A place name; 市 means city, and Kanazawa is in Ishikawa Prefecture.

0.4.n: Links the place name to its local cuisine.

0.5.n: Combines with 料理 to describe food traditional to a particular area.

0.6.n: Together, 郷土料理 means a traditional local dish or regional cuisine.

0.8.n: 治部 belongs to the dish name 治部煮; it does not name an ingredient.

0.9.n: 煮 completes the dish name 治部煮 and indicates simmering.

0.10.n: Identifies 治部煮 as the object of 作ります.

0.11.n: Polite form of 作る; here it announces the planned cooking.

1.0.n: 治部 is the first part of the dish name 治部煮, not a separate ingredient.

1.1.n: 煮 is the ending of the dish name 治部煮.

1.2.n: Marks 治部煮 as the topic being explained.

1.3.n: Combines with 肉 to name the meat normally used in this dish.

1.4.n: Follows 鴨 to form 鴨肉, identifying the ingredient.

1.5.n: Identifies 鴨肉 as the object of 使う.

1.6.n: Plain form of the verb; here it describes the dish's usual preparation.

1.7.n: In のです, の presents the preceding statement as background for the next point.

1.8.n: Adds politeness as part of のです, rather than acting as a separate is here.

1.9.n: Connects the usual ingredient to the contrasting substitution in the next line.

2.0.n: Refers to this particular cooking demonstration.

2.1.n: Highlights 今回, contrasting this version with the usual recipe.

2.2.n: Specifies the animal in 鶏もも肉, distinguishing chicken thigh from other thigh meat.

2.3.n: Combines もも, thigh, with 肉, meat.

2.4.n: Marks 鶏もも肉 as the ingredient used to make the dish.

2.5.n: 作って + いきます politely presents cooking as a process that will unfold from now.

3.0.n: Introduces the first step of the recipe.

3.1.n: Combines 鶏, chicken, with 肉, meat, referring to the thigh meat already mentioned.

3.2.n: Identifies 鶏肉 as the object of 切ったら.

3.3.n: 大 indicates size here: 一口大 is the size of one mouthful.

3.4.n: Marks 一口大 as the resulting size after cutting.

3.5.n: 切る becomes 切ったら; this form introduces a step to finish before the next action.

4.0.n: Names the coating ingredient; 小麦 means wheat and 粉 means powder.

4.1.n: Identifies 小麦粉 as the object of つける; the chicken receiving it is left unstated.

4.2.n: The て-form of つける plus ください makes a polite request to apply the flour.

0.lit: Today, as for, Ishikawa Prefecture, Kanazawa City's local dish, Jibuni, will make.
0.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject; 作ります politely announces what the speaker will make.

1.lit: Jibuni, as for, duck meat uses, the explanation is, but…
1.tip: のですが gives background politely while setting up a contrast with what follows.

2.lit: This time, as for, with chicken thigh meat, will proceed to make.
2.tip: で marks the ingredient used, while 作っていきます introduces the cooking process ahead.

3.lit: First, chicken meat, into bite-sized pieces, once you have cut…
3.tip: In recipe instructions, たら often means once you have done this, rather than a hypothetical if.

4.tip: The chicken is understood from context, so the sentence only names the flour being applied.
